summary: Wei-ming Tu works in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Tunghai and Harvard universities, he held positions at Princeton, UC Berkeley, East-West Center, Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996-2008), Harvard University (1999-2010), and Peking University.
Weijue Shi was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Linyuan, Lingshuan, and Lingyuan in 1963. He founded Lin Quan Temple in 1987, Chung Tai Shan, and Chung Tai Buddhist Institute in 1993.

Weiqiang Wang specializes in linguistics, tibetology, and history/archaeology. He earned a PhD from Guangdong University of Foreign Studies, where he became an associate professor in 2005, and was attested as a researcher at China Tibetology Research Center in 2012.
Weirong Shen works in tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held a post at Renmin University of China around 2006 and has taught at the University of Hong Kong.
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under supervisor Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Weizhong Huang is a tibetology and history/archaeology scholar. He held a post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and serves as a professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

Weldon South Coblin specializes in sinology, linguistics, and tibetology. He studied under Fang-Kuei Li and spent his career at the University of Iowa, serving as professor from around 1973 to 2014 and becoming professor emeritus in 2014.
Wen-ling Jane works in Buddhist studies and tibetology. She studied under Lozang Jamspal and earned a PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2009).

Wenbiao Mai works in indology and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Hamburg, and Peking University (PhD), and served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned a PhD from Stanford under Michel Strickmann, Seizan Yanagida, and Hidehiko Koga, and held posts at Barnard College and the University of Calgary.

Wendy Doniger specializes in indology, religious studies, and history. She earned doctorates under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard and Robert Charles Zaehner at Oxford, and served as a distinguished service professor at the University of Chicago from 1978.
Wenjiang Ding worked in history/archaeology and other fields. He studied at Peking University and under Qichao Liang, later holding a post at Peking University from around 1931 to 1934.

Wenjie Duan worked in history/archaeology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and Central Academy of Fine Arts, he held several leadership roles at Dunhuang Academy between 1946 and 1998, including director and honorary director.

Wenjie Qin is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu and studied under Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.
Wenzhuo Shi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who has been affiliated with Ghent University as a PhD student and researcher from 2022 to at least 2026.

Werner Abraham was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna. He held positions at UIUC, Tübingen, and Groningen (appointed professor in 1971), with later guest professorships in Cologne, Vienna, Lund, and Munich.

Werner Georg Kümmel was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (around 1932-1951), Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (around 1951-1952), and the University of Marburg (around 1952-1973).
Werner Handt was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen in 1900 under the supervision of Richard von Garbe.
Werner Knobl is a scholar of indology and linguistics who studied under Paul Thieme and served as a lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2001-2007).

Werner Schulemann worked in tibetology and pharmacology. He completed doctorates at Breslau and Freiburg, worked at IG Farben, and was a professor at the University of Düsseldorf (1931) and the University of Bonn (1938-1955).
